case.question: Compare relevant competitors in Dubai and Abu Dhabi and propose our positioning.
expected: Differentiation clearly labeled as a proposal

answer.headline: Curated evidence covers Papa Johns branch footprints in both cities plus UAE-wide pizza prices, and one Dubai Levantine-style pizza price point; positioning can be drafted provisionally, but kebab-sandwich rival sets and Abu Dhabi price points are a research gap.

items.text: Papa Johns publicly lists Dubai pizza branches at Al Ghurair Centre (Al Muraqqabat), Deira City Centre (Port Saeed), Al Barsha Mall, and Marina Diamond near Dubai Marina Metro.
Papa Johns publicly lists Abu Dhabi branches at Abu Dhabi Mall (Al Zahiyah), ADNOC 913 Khalidiya, and Al Wahda Mall (Al Manhal), covering mall, corniche-side and central-island catchments.

On the UAE web menu, Papa Johns lists its meat-led All The Meats and Butter Chicken pizzas at AED 33 (8in), AED 50 (10in) and AED 69 (13in), plus Papa's Solo Meal at AED 37 and Meal for Two at AED 69; the store directory states shared menus and prices across branches in both cities.

A Dubai JBR delivery listing shows Allo Beirut pizzas at AED 38 (Margherita) and AED 40 (Pepperoni) — a Levantine-positioned operator pricing pizza above the entry tier of the mainstream chains at that branch and channel.
Branch listings show a business lists an address; they do not establish current trading, sales, market share, footfall, or an available unit. Treat branch counts as footprint evidence only.

sections.title: Competitive map and where we can differ

items.text: The evidence-backed competitive set is a national chain with installed multi-branch pizza capacity in both cities and menu breadth beyond pizzas, plus at least one Levantine-style operator selling pizza via delivery in a Dubai marina-side district.

Our Jordanian meat-forward pizza plus kebab sandwiches is a narrower format than the chain's broad pizza-and-sides menu; the differentiation available from the concept itself is (a) shawarma/kebab-style spiced meats on pizza rather than generic deli meats, and (b) a sandwich-pizza pairing that the observed chain menu does not evidence.
This is not proof of an uncontested niche: no retrieved source enumerates all kebab or shawarma sandwich operators in either city, so claims of uniqueness would be unsupported.

Proposed positioning, conditional on site checks: a Jordanian kebab-and-meat-pizza brand positioned on freshly grilled kebab meat used across both pizza and sandwiches, sold as single-portion and small-group meals — a format that pairs naturally with delivery-led and compact in-line units rather than mall food-court reliance, which is where the observed chain density sits. Validate before committing.

Proposed differentiators to test: named Jordanian spice/grill preparation, meat-to-cheese ratio, a combo of one personal pizza plus one kebab sandwich, and transparent portion specification (diameter and meat weight) against the observed listings that omit portion detail.

Dubai: the observed chain footprint spans Deira/Al Muraqqabat, Port Saeed, Al Barsha and Marina Diamond. Proposed site screen: establish our own kebab-sandwich price and operator evidence for each district before choosing between dense older-Dubai trade corridors (Deira, Al Muraqqabat) and residential/marina areas, rather than assuming which is stronger.

Abu Dhabi: observed chain presence clusters around Abu Dhabi Mall, Khalidiya and Al Wahda Mall. Proposed site screen: shortlist standalone or in-line locations in Al Zahiyah, Al Khalidiyah or Al Manhal and separately price-check against nearby kebab/shawarma operators, since our curated Abu Dhabi evidence has no sandwich competitor set at all.

Research gap: about half of our retrieved records were duplicates of shared UAE price items, so the Abu Dhabi competitor pool here is chain-only. Treat this comparison as incomplete and re-research before a final positioning decision.

sections.title: Reference points for our own pricing work

items.text: Observed reference points (all need rechecking before use): chain pizzas AED 33/50/69 by size, chain bundles AED 37 and AED 69, and a Dubai Levantine-branch pizza at AED 38-40. These are single-channel, single-branch observations, not city averages and not a target band for our menu.

Proposed method: build our own menu price ladder from our recipe costs, then test it against these reference points by size and by order occasion (single meal vs two-person bundle), rather than copying competitor price points directly. Portion sizes on our pizzas should be stated explicitly since the observed competitor listings leave size detail partly unspecified.

assumptions: The business is a Jordanian-origin operator whose core products are meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches, targeting Dubai and Abu Dhabi; all other profile fields (budget, rent budget, branch format, audience, positioning, opening date) are unset.
No branch format has been chosen, so site suggestions are conditional and require site-level checks.
Observed competitor prices are as listed on the named channels on the checked date and were not verified at checkout.
next_steps: Collect our own menu with recipe-level food and packaging costs for each pizza and sandwich SKU so prices can be set bottom-up rather than benchmarked only against competitor listings.

Run a manual competitor audit in 4-6 candidate districts (two in Dubai, two in Abu Dhabi, plus one secondary each) recording kebab/shawarma operators, pizza operators, portion specs, delivery-channel prices and fulfilment mode; curated evidence does not supply this.
Re-verify the observed Papa Johns and Allo Beirut prices on the live menu or delivery app at the specific branch nearest each candidate site before using them in any pricing decision.

If you can supply average order revenue, per-order food, packaging and other variable costs, delivery share and commission, monthly fixed costs and operating days, I can compute contribution and break-even for a chosen site — all eight inputs must come from you, not assumptions.

[2](<https://www.papajohns.ae/menu>)
- **Fact:** A Dubai JBR delivery listing shows Allo Beirut pizzas at AED 38 \(Margherita\) and AED 40 \(Pepperoni\) — a Levantine-positioned operator pricing pizza above the entry tier of the mainstream chains at that branch and channel. [3](<https://deliveroo.ae/en/menu/dubai/jbr/allo-beirut-jbr>)

Validate before committing. [1](<https://www.papajohns.ae/stores>)
- **Proposal:** Proposed differentiators to test: named Jordanian spice/grill preparation, meat-to-cheese ratio, a combo of one personal pizza plus one kebab sandwich, and transparent portion specification \(diameter and meat weight\) against the observed listings that omit portion detail. Proposed site screen: establish our own kebab-sandwich price and operator evidence for each district before choosing between dense older-Dubai trade corridors \(Deira, Al Muraqqabat\) and residential/marina areas, rather than assuming which is stronger. [1](<https://www.papajohns.ae/stores>)

Proposed site screen: shortlist standalone or in-line locations in Al Zahiyah, Al Khalidiyah or Al Manhal and separately price-check against nearby kebab/shawarma operators, since our curated Abu Dhabi evidence has no sandwich competitor set at all.
